# Edwin Trigos | Software Architect & Full Stack Developer

> Portfolio of Edwin Trigos — Tech Lead and .NET Developer specializing in .NET, SQL Server, Clean Architecture, and financial systems. 5+ years building production systems. Bilingual technical blog (ES/EN). Remote from Bucaramanga, Colombia.

Technologies: .NET 8+, C#, SQL Server, Dapper, Clean Architecture, React 19, TypeScript, PHP/Laravel, AWS, Flutter, Docker, Java/Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Azure, Cloudflare Workers, IndexedDB, Playwright, Vitest.

## Blog — Technical Architecture Articles

### Si tu agente usa mal una herramienta, revisa primero el nombre, la descripción y lo que le devuelves
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/una-herramienta-para-un-agente-es-una-api

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: If Your Agent Misuses a Tool, Look First at Its Name, Its Description and What It Returns

When an agent picks the wrong function or invents a parameter, the model gets the blame. I argue the tool deserves the first look: the model decides from a name, a description and whatever you return, like a newcomer in a hurry. Four design moves you can apply this week, what I did in a product of my own, and what good tool design does not fix.

### Por qué importa más lo que le dejas leer al modelo que la forma en que redactas la petición
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/el-contexto-es-presupuesto

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Why What You Let the Model Read Matters More Than How You Word the Request

When a session with a model turns out expensive or wrong, people review how the request was worded. I argue the lever is somewhere else: in what is allowed into the context window, because whatever goes in once is paid for again on every turn and also competes for the model's attention. Four moves for keeping things out, what each one risks, and which part of this is about cost and which is about quality.

### Revisé 56 notas de la memoria de mis agentes y todas figuraban como activas, incluso una que decía estar reemplazada

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: I Checked 56 Notes in My Agents' Memory and Every One Was Listed as Active, Even One That Said It Had Been Replaced

Giving an agent notes that survive between sessions is easy; keeping them true is the hard part. I went through a sample of 56 notes from my own agent memory: every one is listed as active, including one whose title says it was superseded, and every correction I found was written by hand. Four practices for storing less and trusting with a date, and what my sample cannot prove.

### Antes de cambiar de modelo, revisa las reglas y las comprobaciones que le pusiste a tu agente
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/el-modelo-es-la-parte-facil-el-arnes-decide

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Before You Switch Models, Look at the Rules and Checks You Put Around Your Agent

With a coding agent, the outcome depends less on the model than on the harness around it: the rules it reads, what it may touch, how its work is checked, when it has to stop, and how the task is split. Four failures from my own work with agents, all fixed by changing something around the model, three pieces you can add this week, and two questions for telling which rule is dead weight.

### Escribe frases que se entiendan solas, porque un asistente de AI las va a sacar de tu página
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/tu-proximo-lector-es-un-modelo

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Write Sentences That Make Sense on Their Own, Because an AI Assistant Will Lift Them Out of Your Page

An assistant answering a question about a professional or a product does not hand over the page it read: it hands over two or three sentences taken from it. I argue that whoever publishes should write sentences that keep their meaning outside the page, with the number next to its method, and I show it with this site, where a reader that does not run JavaScript gets only the summary of each post. This is an argument from mechanism: I have no data showing that writing this way changes how often a model cites this site.

### Por qué un botón de aprobar no basta cuando la AI propone cambios en tus datos
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/la-ai-propone-una-transaccion-decide

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Why an Approve Button Is Not Enough When AI Proposes Changes to Your Data

In a product built on a language model, the model's output should be a proposal that changes nothing by itself. What changes the data is a deterministic step: a person confirms and a transaction with its own guards does the writing. In my case there was a human in the loop and the loop had a double-approval race; the transaction fixed it, not the prompt. I also say when the gate is unnecessary and what happens when nobody reads what they confirm.

### Por qué a un agente de AI le entrego una prueba que falla antes que una buena descripción

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Why I Hand an AI Agent a Failing Test Before a Good Description

What an AI agent produces is bounded by the check it works against, and not by how well the request is worded. A prompt describes the goal; a test that fails before the work starts defines it. How this site is built on that rule, a ladder for placing each request, and three cases of my own where a wrong check was satisfied to the letter.

### Reemplacé 40 archivos SVG por un componente propio: el blog pesa 22 kB más y aun así fue la decisión correcta
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/figuras-interactivas-en-lugar-de-svg

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: I Replaced 40 SVG Files With an In-House Component: the Blog Got 22 kB Heavier and It Was Still the Right Call

The 21 figures on this blog were 40 hand-written SVG files: they ignored the dark theme, shrank on a phone, and nearly all of them existed twice, once per language. I replaced them with an in-house component that draws from a typed description and plays step by step. Total JavaScript and CSS after gzip went from 444,549 to 466,634 bytes. This case study covers what those 22,085 bytes bought, why a chart library was the wrong tool, and how the work was split among AI agents.

### Puedes pedirle once rondas de revisión a la AI, pero nada reemplaza diez minutos usando el producto como un usuario de verdad
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/once-rondas-de-revision-no-son-un-usuario

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: You Can Ask AI for Eleven Rounds of Review, but Nothing Replaces Ten Minutes of Using the Product Like a Real User

One more review round of the same kind finds less each time, and some defects it never finds, because every reviewer reads the same material with the same means. On a project of my own, 44 adversarial review passes applied 47 findings and missed the two defects that showed up in five minutes of use. More review is not a different view: before paying for a round, ask what is different about whoever runs it.

### Por qué un caso que mediste le sirve más al lector que tu lista de habilidades

A skills list reads the same whether it was written by someone who masters the tool, someone who used it for a week, or someone who is lying. A case with a measurement and its method gives the reader something to rerun. This essay argues for the second using this site as its only evidence, and says plainly what it lacks: any data on whether publishing this way brings work.

### Cuando algo falla, empieza por la explicación más barata de descartar, aunque no sea la que parece más probable
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/ordena-las-hipotesis-por-costo-de-refutar

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: When Something Breaks, Start With the Explanation That Is Cheapest to Rule Out, Even if It Is Not the Likeliest

When something breaks, the usual move is to test the explanation that seems most likely. I argue the order should also weigh what each one costs to rule out, and that the explanation the symptom hands you is the one nobody tests, because it does not feel like a hypothesis. A log saying a provider was not answering could be refuted with one reading; what it invited me to do cost far more.

---

### Antes de cambiar algo que heredaste, escribe qué hace hoy para saber después qué rompiste
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/antes-de-cambiar-lo-que-heredaste

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Before You Change Something You Inherited, Write Down What It Does Today So You Can Tell Later What You Broke

Chesterton's fence asks you to understand why something is there before you remove it. With inherited things that reason is rarely available; the behavior is. I argue that recording what something does today, in a form that can contradict you later, is a rule for leading change more than a testing technique. For systems I have my own evidence; for processes and teams it is an extension by analogy, and I say so.

### Ahora que la AI escribe código rápido, lo que te frena es cuánto puedes confiar en tus pruebas
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/con-ai-el-cuello-de-botella-son-tus-pruebas

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: Now That AI Writes Code Fast, What Slows You Down Is How Much You Can Trust Your Tests

When writing code gets cheap, the scarce thing is being able to trust what verifies it. A suite that runs against stand-ins for reality approves what it does not understand, and every line an assistant writes amplifies that error. Three cases of my own, the DORA 2024 figures, and four rules for knowing what your tests actually ran against.

### Si un arreglo hace pasar la prueba, deja escrito qué problema tapa
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/el-arreglo-que-funciona-no-decide

**Published**: 2026-11-17 | **Language**: ES/EN | **Type**: Essay | **English title**: If a Workaround Makes the Test Pass, Write Down What It Is Hiding

A workaround that makes the test pass feels like a decision, and it rarely is one: it switches off the only signal of the defect and leaves behind an example ready to be copied. I saw it in a test suite where every case pushed a timestamp five seconds back, a convention that covered a defect showing up in 13,339 of 20,000 runs. The workaround is sometimes the right call; what gets expensive is leaving it with no note and no owner.

### AsyncLocal<T> no sube al llamador: dos logs que no podían ser ciertos a la vez
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/asynclocal-no-sube-al-llamador

**Published**: 2026-11-10 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: AsyncLocal<T> Does Not Flow Back to the Caller: Two Logs That Could Not Both Be True

A DelegatingHandler captured the HTTP exchange with an external provider and published it by assigning it to an AsyncLocal. Whoever awaited the call always read null. The HttpClient's own log said 200 in milliseconds; my log said no response had arrived. Two irreconcilable accounts of the same call pointed at the capture channel, not the provider: AsyncLocal flows from parent to child, never back.

### Las pruebas InMemory mienten sobre las transacciones
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/pruebas-inmemory-mienten-sobre-transacciones

**Published**: 2026-11-07 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: InMemory Tests Lie About Transactions

In DevManager, a suite of about 400 tests on the EF Core InMemory provider was green while the confirmation of AI proposals, a transaction built around a conditional state change, had never run against the engine. InMemory does not implement transactions, locks, or unique indexes the way SQL Server does. When an independent verifier ran probes against a real SQL Server, it found three blockers the suite could not see.

### Pruebas de caracterización antes de refactorizar: fijar lo que el código hace, no lo que debería hacer
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/pruebas-caracterizacion-antes-de-refactorizar

**Published**: 2026-11-03 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: Characterization Tests Before Refactoring: Pin What the Code Does, Not What It Should Do

Three methods of 167, 161 and 137 lines in an inherited .NET service, and not a single test that executed them. Before touching a line I wrote 16 characterization tests pinning current behavior, including the order of async side effects; then I cut the methods down to 80, 79 and 34 lines. Along the way I learned that "the file shows up in a test" is not coverage, and that a Times.Never on a method the mock does not know is satisfied by the mock, not by the code.

### GETDATE() contra SYSDATETIME(): el reloj que retrocede dos de cada tres veces
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/getdate-vs-sysdatetime-reloj-que-retrocede

**Published**: 2026-10-27 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: GETDATE() vs SYSDATETIME(): The Clock That Runs Backwards Two Times Out of Three

A database test failed intermittently on a guard that requires one event to happen after another. I measured the cause: GETDATE() read right after SYSDATETIME() compares as earlier in 13,339 of 20,000 runs, because datetime rounds to 3.33 ms steps and datetime2 does not. The test was fixed by pushing a timestamp five seconds into the past, which is exactly the fix that corrects nothing; the real correction is one clock and one type end to end.

---

### Trabajo en segundo plano en .NET sin un broker de mensajes
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/trabajo-en-segundo-plano-channel-sin-broker

**Published**: 2026-10-20 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: Background Work in .NET Without a Message Broker

A synchronous call to an external voice-bot provider kept the HTTP request open while the bot dialed. I turned it into enqueue-and-poll with a bounded Channel<T> and a BackgroundService, resolving scoped dependencies from a singleton worker, computing the job phase from columns that already existed, and expiring passively on read with no sweeper process. No broker, no job library, no new infrastructure, and an honest table of what that costs.

Worse: a report certified that every snippet used invented identifiers, and nobody reviewed it because it read like a finished check. This is what I changed in the process.

### El atributo de autorización que ninguna prueba unitaria puede ver
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#blog/article/atributo-autorizacion-invisible-prueba-unitaria

**Published**: 2026-09-26 | **Language**: ES/EN | **English title**: The Authorization Attribute a Unit Test Cannot See

I added an administrative endpoint that replaces an operation only a DBA could previously run, protected by an authorization attribute. The obvious unit test confirmed it green by calling the controller method directly, which is exactly why it proved nothing: that attribute is only ever evaluated by the middleware, never by a bare method call. The honest test needed a real test server and a deliberate mutation of the attribute to prove it measured what it claimed to measure.

## Case Studies — Production Systems

### STARSOL — SaaS Platform for Integrated Risk Management
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2024-Present | **Role**: Cloud Software Architect & Independent Developer
**Stack**: PHP, Laravel, AWS, .NET MAUI, MySQL, Docker, CI/CD

B2B SaaS platform for the solidarity sector covering SARLAFT, SARC, and SIAR risk management. Async architecture with 3 background workers processing jobs simultaneously, decoupling file uploads from the main web server thread. .NET MAUI client app with offline sync. AWS high-availability infrastructure with CI/CD pipelines.

### LOS — Loan Origination System
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2025-2026 | **Role**: Software Architect / Full Stack Developer
**Stack**: .NET 8+, C#, Dapper, SQL Server, Clean Architecture, REST API, JWT, Strategy Pattern

Complete loan origination system built from scratch. Data layer: DDL with 4 logical schemas (cfg/cat/fab/aud), 30+ tables, 23-state state machine, 27 stored procedures. Service layer: REST API with Clean Architecture — repositories per schema, services per domain, controllers per channel (Admin/Store/Web/Handoff). Identity verification via voice bot with catalog-driven decision engine. Biometric fraud detection. INSERT-ONLY audit trail.

**Impact**: 114+ API endpoints across 6 BFF layers (Admin/Core/Store/Web/Handoff/Util). 27 stored procedures in production. 23-state loan lifecycle with full traceability. Automated identity verification via voice bot with manual Plan B as a first-class citizen. Immutable audit trail of all operations. 474/474 tests green after making the risk-data provider configurable, delivered as 3 chained PRs. I then redesigned the operator's case workspace so every action gets its own dialog instead of sharing a generic one, delivered as 10 chained commits of at most 400 lines each and closed with 23 requirements and 117 verified scenarios. An administrative endpoint replaced an operation only a DBA could previously run, delivered as 3 chained PRs, with its guarding permission proven through the real HTTP pipeline rather than a direct method call.

### SOVI — Identity Validation Orchestrator
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026 | **Role**: Software Architect
**Stack**: .NET, C#, SQL Server, Strategy Pattern, REST API

Strategy pattern with two validation strategies: BotValidacionStrategy (voice bot) and ManualValidacionStrategy (human advisor). Catalog-driven decision engine — no hardcoded if/switch. Each bot diagnosis triggers a SystemAction from database catalog. Complete traceability per study with 10+ categorized bot diagnoses.

Credit bureau REST API with resilience patterns (Polly circuit breaker + retry policy). JWT authentication. Structured logging with Serilog. Request/response logging middleware with sensitive field sanitization. Query times reduced from 3s to 400ms through index optimization.

### Portfolio — Hybrid Architecture
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026-Present | **Role**: Frontend Developer & Designer
**Stack**: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, GitHub API, Playwright

Designed a hybrid architecture: curated content layer (STAR-format case studies in TypeScript, work experience, blog) as the primary source of truth, and GitHub API as a secondary activity widget. Implemented native i18n (ES/EN), pixel-art editorial design system with pixel shadows and newspaper typography, and Framer Motion animations. Built with React 19 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4. On top of that I added a second theme selected through `data-theme` —from the editorial newspaper to an interactive XP-style desktop— driven by a WindowManager that owns every rect, clamp and z-order: draggable windows, 8-handle resizing, a Start menu, a taskbar with a utilities tray, tabs inside a single window, and a Help window kept out of the visible registry. I also treated visibility to AI engines as measurable engineering: JSON-LD structured data plus `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, which took an automated GEO audit from 58 to 83/100.

**Impact**: Architecture that prioritizes business impact over source code. NDA-compliant case studies without exposing confidential information. Native i18n without external libraries. Custom design system that visually stands out from generic portfolios. Adding a case study = 1 TypeScript object. The XP desktop was built with strict TDD against a committed Playwright driver —98/98 checks, RED before GREEN on every work unit— and a second committed driver pixel-diffs the newspaper theme across 4 viewports × 2 locales against committed baselines: it demands 0 differing pixels, so the editorial design cannot drift while the second theme evolves.

### Centralized Email Communications API — Single Provider
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2024 | **Role**: Backend Architect / API Designer
**Stack**: .NET 8, C#, Clean Architecture, Dapper, SQL Server, Serilog, Polly, Azure Blob Storage, JWT

**Problem**: 5 independent email sending silos, each system calling the provider directly with its own credentials, retry logic and format. Diagnosing an undelivered email took 30 minutes across 5 servers and 8 mailboxes. Zero cross-system traceability.

**Solution**: One REST API in .NET 8 with Clean Architecture in 4 layers (Api / Application / Domain / Infrastructure). A provider-agnostic IEmailProvider interface in Domain; an application service that validates, applies per-context templates with typed tokens, persists each transaction with its own GUID before calling the provider, and retries with exponential backoff; a typed HttpClient adapter with Polly circuit breaker in Infrastructure. 8 multi-tenant accounts resolved by business context from configuration. Serilog with 3 pipelines and sanitization of attachments, PII and credentials.

**Impact**: Diagnosis time for an undelivered email from 30 minutes to 5 seconds. Zero hardcoded credentials, rotatable without redeploy. Provider change measured in hours, not weeks. Zero orphan emails. 7 REST controllers (one per consumption channel) sharing the same application service.

### Harmony-Music — Cross-Platform Flutter Open Source Music App
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026-Present | **Role**: Open Source Maintainer & Flutter Developer
**Stack**: Flutter 3.44+, Dart, GetX, just_audio, media_kit, audio_service, youtube_explode_dart, Hive, Dio, JNI

**Problem**: The original creator marked the repository as "unmaintained" in December 2025: abandoned dependencies, leftover Gradle migrator flags, runtime crashes (RangeError from indexWhere returning -1), no debugging tools, and an undocumented API (YouTube Music InnerTube) that changed without notice and broke search.

**Solution**: 4-phase triage. (1) Build first — Gradle 8.14, AGP 8.11.1, Kotlin 2.2.20 with modern DSL. (2) Deprecations — 19 commits replacing deprecated Flutter/Material APIs and removing dead packages. (3) Runtime — rewrote search bucketing for the new flat InnerTube format, added indexWhere guards, structured HTTP logging. (4) Tooling — a ResponseRecorder that captures raw responses to disk for offline diffing. Audio via just_audio + media_kit + audio_service + SMTC on 3 platforms with a single Dart API.

**Impact**: ~36 commits in 3 days from "does not compile" to release v1.12.2 with a modern toolchain. Working search with the new InnerTube format. Clean build on Flutter 3.44+. Audio on 3 platforms. Complete documentation, releases and changelog.

### ReaderSS — RSS Reader with Offline Reading and an Edge Relay
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026 | **Role**: Architect & Full Stack Developer
**Stack**: TypeScript, Preact, Vite, IndexedDB, Cloudflare Workers, DOMPurify, Vitest, GitHub Actions

**Problem**: Browsers dropped native RSS support; surviving readers are cloud services that keep your feed list. A browser page cannot fetch an arbitrary feed (CORS), and none of it works offline.

**Solution**: Domain, ports and adapters behind a composition root with IndexedDB as the data layer. A Cloudflare Workers relay solves CORS and adds conditional GET, size and time limits, an SSRF guard re-applied on every redirect hop, and an explicitly non-authenticating origin guard. Parsers for RSS 2.0, RDF, Atom and JSON Feed normalize onto one entry model; DOMPurify sanitisation at a single choke point. OPML import/export, read/unread/starred state with per-field timestamps, per-feed failure reporting.

**Impact**: 787 tests with lint and typecheck clean, and an enforced 70% coverage gate (the last measurement, at 426 tests, gave ~95% statement coverage and a 248 kB raw bundle, 88 kB gzipped). GitHub Actions runs lint, typecheck and tests before deploying to Cloudflare Workers. Public MIT-licensed repository.

### How I build software with AI agents and what they missed
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026-Present | **Role**: Architect & Developer
**Stack**: Claude Code, Gentle AI, Engram, CodeGraph, LLM tool calling, Playwright

**Problem**: An AI agent writes code fast and also states things nobody checked. On ReaderSS, 11 catalogued cases where a comment, a test name or a ticked checkbox said something the code did not do. One comment spoke of "six outcomes" when there were eight, and the coordinating session copied it into its own instructions without counting. Every conversation with an agent starts with no memory of the previous one, across several projects and two computers.

**Solution**: A main session that coordinates and helper agents that each get a bounded task and the exact list of files they may edit. The coordination rules and the review through four independent lenses come from Gentle AI, an open-source project Edwin installed and configured. Engram (memory between sessions) and CodeGraph (code structure) are open tools made by other people. What Edwin wrote: a feature document per large feature with his own sentences quoted, the task list and a log with the evidence (11 of them in this portfolio), nine skills (five in this repository, four in other projects) and 17 Playwright drivers that open the site in a real browser. When the case studies section was rebuilt, the new driver passed 21 of its 48 checks before the change and all 48 after it.

**Impact**: On ReaderSS, 11 review rounds with four lenses (44 passes, 47 findings applied, among them 1 blocker and 4 critical ones) did not see the two defects that left the application unusable. Both were found within minutes of opening it in the browser: the development command did not start the service that fetches the feeds, and a fourth element in a three-column grid pushed the reading pane off the screen. The 423-test suite could not see either. Memory failed too: syncing it between two computers changed the number of each note on every import and the export never deleted old files, so a folder that should have held 473 notes held 1,369 files, about 900 too many. Rules adopted: give a person something they can open early, and never write a figure that was not counted.

### I made this portfolio readable by AI assistants
https://portfolio.edwintrigos.workers.dev/#projects
**Period**: 2026 | **Role**: Frontend Developer
**Stack**: Vite, TypeScript, JSON-LD, Schema.org, llms.txt, RSS

**Problem**: The portfolio is a single-page application: the server sends an almost empty HTML file and the content appears once the browser runs JavaScript. An automated audit of visibility to AI engines gave it 58/100: citability 94, technical 66 (no llms.txt, no sitemap, no canonical URL), structured data 0, presence on other sites 48.

**Solution**: A Vite plugin that, at build time, imports the same content files the application uses and writes the case studies, the articles and the work experience into the HTML (10.6 kB to 68.3 kB). The same plugin generates Schema.org JSON-LD. llms.txt and llms-full.txt, robots.txt, canonical URL and sitemap. Later, one static share page per article, because the routes come after a `#` that a server never sees.

**Impact**: The same audit went from 58 to 83/100 on the same day, with the 14 problems it had found resolved. Technical 66 to 92. Structured data 0 to 99, with 26 Schema.org types. Citability stayed at 94. Presence on other sites stayed at 48 because it depends on work outside the code. According to the audit, server rendering would add 7 technical points and take the total to 86.
